articleTitle: Chilli Quality Classification using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Chilli peppers (Capsicum annuum) are potential commodities in Indonesia that have relatively high economic value. Sorting and grading of chilli peppers after harvesting is very important for separating the post-harvest results to determine whether the chillies are in good or bad conditions. Currently, these activities are still done manually using visual observation. The problem of using this manual method is that the process often becomes time-consuming. Another drawback of utilizing manual methods is that it has often inconsistent results. This study aims to develop a decision support system for classifying the quality of chillies using deep learning. The development of the science and technology of digital image processing makes it possible to sort agricultural and plantation products automatically. In this research, we employ “You Only Look Once” (YOLO) method which is one technique of the deep learning methods that is widely used for image recognition in real-time. Simulation results from the custom model show that the classification accuracy obtained from the simple test is 99.4% and the challenging test is 75.6%.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Environmental Monitoring System for Brunei Peat Swamp Forest
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Brunei Darussalam is largely covered by the tropical rainforest. Around 16% of Brunei total land area is Peatland. This peatland is under the protection of the Heart of Borneo initiative. This peatland forest plays a very important role in the region's rainforest ecosystem. However, this type of forest is vulnerable to fire outbreak, and hence the forest needs to be sustained. By using an Internet of Things (IoT) -based remote monitoring system, peat swamp forest areas can be monitored for long term management and short-term natural disaster preparedness. The proposed monitoring system is a solar-powered system equipped with built-in Long Range (LoRa) network to allow the data collection via a gateway. The system is designed to measure environmental conditions such as soil and water temperature, soil moisture, water level, wind direction and atmospheric humidity and pressure. The data collected by the system is programmed to be displayed on a dashboard which can be viewed remotely by respective agencies. The proposed system has been lab-tested on various conditions of peat soils giving measurement results which are usable for data reference.

articleTitle: A Proof-of-Concept of Farmer-to-Consumer Food Traceability on Blockchain for Local Communities
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Recent pandemic presses importance on the trade of quality produce from local farmers to consumers. Traditionally, farmers rely on middlemen to sell their produce, resulting in occasional price injustice, and the lack of direct communication with their customers who could be interested in learning more about the produce they consume. To provide trusts using technology instead of an intermediary, this paper proposes a design of a blockchain-based food traceability system for local farmers to sell produce to health-aware consumers who could trace the farming activities of the produce they purchase. The system is based on a private blockchain platform, Hyperledger Fabric, that supports farmers, carriers, and consumers. Farm activities can be recorded by farmers. Consumers can view produce history before making a purchase, and track transportation by carriers up until delivery. IoT is integrated to record farming environments and quality of farm during plantation is evaluated. This provides a proof-of-concept of how a blockchain-based system can be implemented for local produce marketplace without the need of intermediary.

articleTitle: Ensemble Learning for Predictive Maintenance on Wafer Stick Machine Using IoT Sensor Data
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Improper maintenance on a machine or system impacts to worsen mean time between failure (MTBF). Manual diagnostic procedures tend to extended downtime at the system breakdown. Machine learning techniques based on the internet of things (IoT) sensor data were proposed to make predictive maintenance to determine system condition, whether it needs to maintain or not. The working component initiates with attribute selection with a correlation ranking filter to rank the most necessary attribute(s) to system condition. In the sequential step, ensemble learning procedures were set to create a predictive maintenance model. Based on a numeric data experiment, wait found that six of wafer stick machine attributes impacting on system condition and a working evaluation on this proposed predictive maintenance model performed better with 95,90% accuracy.

articleTitle: Development of an Aircraft Type Portable Autonomous Drone for Agricultural Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate the design and development of an aircraft type portable autonomous drone suitable for agricultural applications. The portable drone consists of six separate parts that are easily installable within just ten minutes. Moreover, these parts can be fit inside a portable box allowing easy portability. We have integrated a high definition camera with the drone to transmit real-time video of any desired crop's field to the ground control station. To scare the birds and to announce emergency to the farmers, we have installed a loud speaker with the bird-shaped drone. The drone can fly under different altitude varying from 10 to 200 meters. The maximum cruise speed of the drone is 60 kilometers/hour, whereas the maximum endurance time is ~ 30 minutes. The drone can carry ~ 1.4 kilograms of payload (e.g. seeds) and deliver to the farmers when required. The agricultural drone has Return Home feature for autonomous return to the ground control station when its battery voltage reduces down to a certain level or any communication failure is detected. The drone will not only monitor the possible threats of the agricultural fields including diseases and harms caused by birds or other animals but also supply light weight emergency goods to the farmers.

articleTitle: Enhancing Crops Production Based on Environmental Status Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: The suitable crop for a particular location is necessary for agriculture to bring the most productivity. Here we have designed a model that contains prediction and recommendation with machine learning approaches that determines productivity based on the parameters humidity, rainfall, and temperature. For the prediction, we have applied k-nearest neighbor (KNN), support vector machines (SVM), random forest, naive Bayes' classifier and logistic regression, collaborative filtering, and Multi-Condition Filtering algorithms. After training the dataset and applying these algorithms, we have made a comparison of the algorithms by analyzing the precision. On the other hand, for the recommendation, we have applied collaborative filtering and Multi-Condition Filtering algorithms where these algorithms take input parameters. And then, in the collaborative filtering the input parameter is compared with the trained data that is already in the system and filters out the best 5 crops as output based on cosine similarity and Multi-Condition Filtering algorithm categorizes the crop with a different combination of the high, low and moderate ranges of the input parameter and displays the crop accordingly.

articleTitle: Design of Green ERP System Reverse Logistic Module Based on Odoo in Leather Tanning Industry
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Rise of the leather industry in Indonesia since 2018 makes this industry more visible to the market. Along with the increasing development of leather industry, waste that generated will naturally increase. PT. ELCO Indonesia Sejahtera as a company engaged in leather tanning industry (sheep and goat skin) experienced an increase of waste, from the production process and returned products. Currently PT. ELCO Indonesia Sejahtera still input returned products data manually and still have no system integration to manage business process in company. This condition causes company to view asynchronous data for returned products in inventory and company still have no monitoring process for type of products and routing that often occurs error. To solve those problems, management for returned products needs to be done through system due to view data in real-time and have a more optimal monitoring process. The system based on Green Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) with Odoo application by applying reverse logistics concept which aims to manage waste from returned products. This research uses SAP Activate methodology for designing system. The results in this study is system can integrate repair module with other modules such as inventory and manufacturing. And to improve business workflow in the company, reverse logistic module produces monitoring reports in the form of transaction document and graph.

articleTitle: Development of Autonomous UAV Quadcopters using Pixhawk Controller and Its Flight Data Acquisition
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) quadcopter is a copter with four driving motors. It is widely used in various applications including agriculture because the design is simple and the concept of motion is easy to understand. However, currently, the widely sold quadcopters in the Indonesian market are quadcopters that are controlled manually using remote control. In this work, we developed two autonomous UAV quadcopters that can fly autonomously according to two predetermined trajectories, i.e., rectangular and circular trajectories. This preliminary work aims to support various quadcopter applications for smart and precision farming on fix agricultural lands. The trajectories are predetermined in accordance to the landforms and the quadcopters are expected to follow these trajectories autonomously. This study has succeeded in building two autonomous quadcopter with different specifications: quadcopter type F450 and quadcopter type F330. The experimental testing results show that the average latitude and longitude mean squared error of the quadcopter flight is 6.79×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-10</sup> for the F450 quadcopter and 1.45×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup> for the F330 quadcopter. The flight sensors data obtained in this study is available to be used for research and educational purposes. Please contact the authors for access to the UAV flight data.

articleTitle: Image Processing for Diagnosis Rice Plant Diseases Using the Fuzzy System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: The biggest challenge for farmers in producing quality rice plants is rice plant disease. To reduce the impact caused by rice disease, early detection is needed. Farmers usually detect rice diseases based on the characteristics that appear in rice plants. Unfortunately, diagnoses made by farmers often vary due to differences in experience and knowledge. Rice plant disease diagnosis through the laboratory is considered less effective because it requires long time and a large amount of cost. This study aims to build a system for detecting rice diseases that can be used quickly with accurate results. The system was built using a fuzzy system with ten inputs. This input is the result of the extraction of rice plant images, i.e. contrast, correlation, energy, homogeneity, average, variance, kurtosis, entropy, standard deviation, and skewness. The fuzzification process is carried out using the Gauss membership function, the fuzzy inference is done using the Sugeno method, and the defuzzification process uses the weight average method. Output variables are classified into three sets, i.e. Bacterial leaf blight, Brown spot, and Leaf smut. Graphical user interface was used to improve the user experience in using fuzzy system. The accuracy of the detection system of rice disease produced was 94,792% based on training data and 91,667% based on testing data.

articleTitle: Multi-UAV Coordination for Crop Field Surveillance and Fertilization
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: In multi-UAV coordination, zig-zag method has been shown to be the most efficient way to surveil an area in terms of spatial distributions. However, this method is not robust to system failure. This paper proposes a method for Multi-UAV coordination that uses dynamic path planning based on search-attack mission self-organized algorithm (SAMSOA). SAMSOA is derived from distributed Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) approach and was originally used to solve search-attack missions. In this paper, we modify SAMSOA for simultaneous surveillance and fertilization. Algorithm evaluation is achieved by comparing SAMSOA to the conventional zig-zag method in two scenario environments where; (1) all UAV's can work normally and; (2) where some UAV's are broken. The performance is analyzed according to the total required time to complete all missions. The simulation result demonstrates, in all scenarios SAMSOA method requires shorter completion time compared with the conventional zig-zag method.

articleTitle: An Initial Framework of Dynamic Software Product Line Engineering for Adaptive Service Robot
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Service robot has its challenge to adapt on new tasks based on instruction or environment. Such conditions need to reconfigure or reorganize to obtain new system capabilities. However, most common service robot, especially the one that gives services to help human to deliver food or non medical stuffs in an elderly house, suffers on its task flexibility. Unlike a human, robot system needs to be reconfigured to have a new task which may interrupt its services because of this event. To this, we need a technique to handle adaptive tasks that is flexible to change the robot tasks that do not create delay. Dynamic software product line provides a mechanism to reconfigure a system to have different capabilities based on the core assets of the system, such as software that supports and controls the hardware components in a robotic system. In this work, we make use of the dynamic software product line to create a flexible method that enables a service robot to adapt on its new tasks. In order to define the change of tasks, we model the transformation of task using a transition state which has constraints as a trigger. Other than that, the request of change may also have resulted by forcing an interrupt mechanism. To demonstrate the capability of our approach, the proof of concept using Robotic Operating System will be presented.

articleTitle: Implementation of Breadth-First Search Parallel to Predict Drug-Target Interaction in Plant-Disease Graph
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Degenerative diseases are often treated by using chemical drugs. But the use of chemical drugs has the risk to cause side effects. Herbal medicine has smaller side effects compared to the chemical drugs. The development of drugs for degenerative diseases requires large costs with several side effects and risks. Drug repurposing can minimize costs, risks, and time needed to develop drug. The target-based objectives of computational method was used to search for compound-protein similarities and predict drug-protein interactions. This research uses breadth-first search algorithm that was implemented in parallel computation. The algorithm was compared in performance by using sequential and parallel computing. The results show that the parallelization based on BFS using 4 threads size require 46.299 seconds to complete searching process and obtain speed up of 51.33 times compared to the sequential algorithm.

articleTitle: Estimating Crop Water Stress of Sugarcane in Indonesia Using Landsat 8
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Water-deficit stress is one of the critical problems in the sugarcane (Saccharum spp.) production that affect plant growth and productivity. Water stress alters a variety of physiological processes in sugarcane that interfere with sugarcane spectral response. In this paper, we employ remote sensing technology to estimate the level of water stress of sugarcane plantation at PTPN X by using a crop water stress index (CWSI). We observe drought stress response from land surface temperature (LST) to calculate CWSI using a split-window algorithm. Landsat 8 satellite imagery and water vapor data from the MODIS-Aqua satellite were used for detecting the sugarcane water stress index by integrating CWSI and Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI). The results indicated that CWSI and NDVI can be effectively used to estimate the level of water stress of sugarcane. The results would be useful in irrigation management to schedule irrigation of sugarcane fields.

articleTitle: A Design of Traceability System in Coffee Supply Chain based on Hierarchical Cluster Analysis Approach
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Traceability systems are a concern in the current food supply chain mainly due to food safety issues. Related traceability problem in the supply chain is the risk of changes in the information on coffee products presented on the consumer's side, thereby reducing their trust in information and customer loyalty on the product. This study aims to analyze the business process of the real-world situation in coffee commodity supply chains, generate a dataset from these observations, and to propose a traceability system design using the clustering approach. The methodology in this research consisted of field observation and desk study, multicollinearity analysis, and hierarchical cluster analysis and formulation. The results show that the activities occurring in the coffee commodity supply chain take place between 4 stakeholders, which is indicated by UML. The generated dataset is then compared in correlation so that four variables are selected to use as references in designing the traceability system. Finally, the clustering method shows 4 clusters, where every 2 clusters in 2 existing varieties. The resulting cluster has been able to interpret as much as 84.83% of the dataset tested.

articleTitle: Design of Smart System For Fruit Packinghouse Management in Supply Chain
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Packinghouse management is an integration of a series of business processes and good handling practices. Many previous studies have discussed using technology and methods in each business process at the packinghouse but have not been integrated and are still focused on data input, data processing, and reporting. This research proposes the design of technology and computational integration in a business process called the Smart System for Fruit Packinghouse Management (SPHM) with the aim of accurate fruit classification, product selection, and delivery model to be sent appropriately, selection of appropriate packaging, stock optimization, reduce costs, increase sales and profits, and customer loyalty. This system consists of four sub-systems are Smart Logistic System, Smart Indexing System, Smart Packaging System, and Smart Storage System. Integration of technology and computing proposed are RFID, Computer Vision, Vis / NIR, IoT, WSN, AHP, GA, Topsis, RNN, LS-SVM, ABC, HOG, SPA, CARS, SVM, SVR, Fuzzy Logic Control, Time Series Analysis Techniques, and MLFANN.

articleTitle: CNN with Multi Stage Image Data Augmentation Methods for Indonesia Rare and Protected Orchids Classification
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Image classification of Indonesian rare and protected orchids is one of the solutions to prevent illegal trade, especially in online commerce that uses images as one of the display features. Image classification using deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is a major breakthrough at this time where the extraction feature is done automatically through a series of convolution layers. Deep CNN requires a lot of training data to produce a good classification result. Image data of Indonesian rare and protected orchids are relativHeruely difficult to obtain when searched through relevant sources to avoid inaccurate information. In this paper, we propose a new approach of multi-stage image data augmentation to overcome limited data problem in deep CNN for Indonesian rare and protected orchids image classification. Image data augmentation method using basic image augmentation divided into geometric transformation and distortion injection. ResNet with transfer learning as CNN model is used for the classification. The proposed system is experimentally evaluated in the form of data augmentation methods combination such as stage 1 and stage 2 augmented dataset and results show its convincing performance compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of IoT Connectivity using LoRaWAN for Vending Machine Network
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Automatic vending machine can be one of the solutions to provide an optimal distribution as one of the keys factor to controlling the prices of basic commodities. It can be connected with LoRaWAN as IoT connectivity which has wide area coverage, low power, and delay tolerant. This paper tested and evaluated the IoT connectivity using LoRaWAN for a vending machine network. The tested connectivity range are 0, 200, 400, and 600 meters and we did not take varying condition of any varying weather condition. The performance of Time on-air, Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI), Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR), and Throughput are 1.84 seconds, 87%, -87.75 dBm, and 374.59 bit/s, respectively.

articleTitle: Predicting Methane Emission from Paddy Fields with Limited Soil Data by Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Paddy fields with flooded water are commonly known as the main source of methane (CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>) emission. Measurement of methane gas is complicated and costly due to utilizing advanced instrumentation such as Gas Chromatography (GC). In addition, some soil parameter data that is effected on methane emissions were sometimes limited. The current study proposed the artificial neural network (ANN) models to predict methane emission from paddy fields using soil parameters of soil moisture (SM), soil temperature (Ts) and soil electrical conductivity (EC). The models were performed based on the experimental data in one planting season during 20 January to 13 May 2018. The ANN models were developed by backpropagation learning algorithm. The sigmoid function was used as an activation function with three layer, i.e. input, hidden and output layers. There were six ANN models with different input parameters. Model 1 with three input parameters (SM, Ts, EC) was the best model with highest R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (0.97) and lowest RMSE (32.9 mg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/d). However, the model needs more input parameters. The Model 2 can be used as an alternative to predict methane emission if there were only two measured parameter, i.e., SM and Ts. This model was fairly satisfied as indicated by R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.64 and moderate RMSE of 122.8 mg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/d.

articleTitle: Drug-Target Visualization on IJAH Analytics Using Sankey Diagram
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: IJAH Analytics is a website that provides information about herbs and can predict the efficacy of several herbal plant formulations. This research focuses on developing the IJAH Analytics front-end module and improving the Graphical User Interface (GUI). The GUI implements recommendations for improvements based on usability tests that have been carried out in IJAH Analytics version 2, especially in multipartite graphic visualization. Improvements made include making graphics more responsive, reducing crossed edges, and giving color to graphic visualizations. Visualization is implemented using the Google Chart library to display on a website. The development of the front-end module uses the Prototyping method, and the usability test of satisfaction parameters uses the System Usability Scale (SUS) questionnaire. IJAH Analytics is successfully developed in 3 iterations and resulted in an average SUS score of 69.5. The third version of IJAH Analytics provides a better and more interactive display of use and helps in finding herbal formulas.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network For Estimation Nutrient Utilization Based on Chemical Composition on Ruminant Animal Feed
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: The production of ruminant livestock is used to meet the needs of human food. The productivity of ruminants is determined by the feed given. Therefore, a proper feeding strategy is needed. This research aims to estimate the nutrient utilization of ruminant forage plants based on chemical content using Artificial Neural Network (ANN). Chemical content used as the estimator is the main analysis category; meanwhile, ruminant nutritive values are predicted from our model. A total of 136 species of forage plants were obtained from http://www.feedipedia.org. Data were divided into training and testing data using K-fold cross-validation with k=3. The process of estimation was performed using the ANN structure with several variation numbers of neurons in the hidden layer from 4, 6, and 8. As a result, the ANN structure built could estimate the nutrient properly, indicated by small values of RMSE (3.33) revealed from ANN structure with four neurons. The determination coefficient (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) from this ANN model more than 0.50 for all output, except in the production of Metabolizable energy, which was 0.49.

articleTitle: Study and Experiment of Generalized Frequency Division Multiplexing Implementation using USRP and LabVIEW
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: The 5G is not only improving mobile broadband experience but also increasing massively connected devices. Hence, the dynamic and flexible spectrum allocation for the devices is essential. Generalized Frequency Division Multiplexing (GFDM) is one of the promising techniques that meets the above requirements. However, most of the researches are conducted based on mathematical modeling and software simulation. This paper develops GFDM implementation for transmission and reception over the air (OTA) using Universal Software Radio Peripheral (USRP) RIO 2942 and LabVIEW. The spectrum analyzer used is to verify the received signals simultaneously. Experimental results show that GFDM signals are successfully received and confirmed by the spectrum analyzer. Moreover, the GFDM technique can perform transmission by selecting specific subcarriers. The power gap between selected and non-selected subcarriers is -40 dB meaning that out of band emission complies with the 3GPP standard.

articleTitle: Web Service-based Automata Testing: A Case Study on Online Airline Reservation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Information exchange between organizations, associates, and customers is essential for the success of any type of business. Thus, a web service (can be software, application, or cloud technology) is being used for backing communication between application-to-application and solving the interoperability problem. It offers homogeneous web protocols to interoperate, interconnect, and exchange data messaging with numerous applications with HTML, XML, WSDL, SOAP, and other open standards. In this study, we develop a framework to demonstrate how the idea of web services can be utilized for online airline reservations by utilizing the finite automata computational model. The model is a fundamental computing model that presents sufficient behaviour of the service based on its user consideration or inquiries. To express the transition flow of an online airline reservation with the given desired input, the nondeterministic finite automata (NFA) is being used. For the validation, the NFA is being converted to the Deterministic Finite Automata (DFA) to make out the anticipated patterns. The entire framework process was carried out using the Java Formal Languages and Automata Package (JFLAP) simulation tool and was tested with precise and valid simulating inputs.

articleTitle: Implementation of Recursive Least Square for Basic Piano Chords Noise Reduction
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Recursive least square has been applied and researched for noise reduction of various kinds of noise. The applications showed a fast convergence and high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). This noise reduction algorithm will be implemented in EPCP (enhanced pitch class profile) to reduce audience noise in piano live concert. The noisy piano chord signals are recorded using a smartphone for a second with a sampling rate of 48 kilohertz. The crowd noise will be reduced by using RLS. The quality of noise reduction is determined by the accuracy of chord classification using EPCP for feature extraction and kNN for pattern matching. Observation on the effect of tap-weight filter length of RLS on the accuracy of chord recognition is also carried out in this paper. Tap-weight filter of size 100 yielded the best result with 92.9% accuracy. The misclassification of D chord is caused by the increasing of A# tone chroma value as the result of noise reduction. This calls for further research on the effect of tap-weight filter length on the spectral element of the noise-reduced signal.

articleTitle: Application of Gravitational Search Algorithm on the Modified Compartmental Absorption and Transit Model for Predicting Oral Drug Absorption
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: The rate of oral drug absorption can be predicted using the compartmental absorption and transit (CAT) model. In this paper, the CAT model has been modified by combining the dissolution constant in seven compartments in the small intestine to define the plasma concentration of the oral drug, Atenolol. The simulations were performed using the MATLAB program and optimized by gravitational search algorithm (GSA) technique. Based on the results of the simulation the prediction of plasma concentration of Atenolol at doses of 25, 50, and 100 mg, the MCAT model with GSA optimization has a better prediction as compared to the MCAT simulation only. The determination coefficient values (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) are increased from the range of 80% to more than 90% and show that the simulation results fit very well with the experimental data. The inclusion of GSA helps to optimize the MCAT model in predicting the plasma concentration of drug in the absorption, distribution, and metabolism phase (the first 8 hours after drug administration).

articleTitle: Implementation of Borda Clustering to Form Zakat Receiving Villages Clusters Based on Region Potency in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Indonesia has a huge potential of zakat funds up to IDR 286 trillion. This is a positive impact of the large moslem population that reached 216.66 million in 2016. However, the absorption and distribution of zakat funds have not been maximized, for example in 2015 the absorption of zakat was IDR 3.70 trillion and the distributed fund were only 61.61 percent. The utilization of region's potential data can be an alternative approach to expand zakat distribution. This research implements Borda Clustering algorithm on the 2011 Potential Village Skyline Data from the Central Statistics Agency to produce priority area clusters of zakat receiver in Indonesia. Evaluations using the Silhouette Score against the cluster resulted 0.72 in range of -1 to +1. The regional clusters prioritized in obtaining zakat funds are mostly in Papua, Nangro Aceh Darrusalam, and West Papua Province. The results of the clusters can be used as suggestion for the zakat management organization to maximize the distribution of zakat funds.

articleTitle: Development of GPU-Accelerated Pre-processing Chain for LAPAN-A2 Multispectral Imagery
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: This paper reported the development of a newly accelerated chain for pre-processing raw data acquired by LAPAN-A2 multispectral sensor. The acceleration schema was achieved by making full use of Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) to handle parallel processing in raw data encoding, image demosaicing, and radiometric-geometric correction stages. Based on the experiment conducted on NVIDIA GeForce GT 1030 GPU card, the developed chain was found capable of resulting level-1 imagery accurately of up to 3.72 times faster than that of similar implementation on Core-i7 8700 CPU. It was also found that the GPU device boosted the demosaicing stage more than 10 times faster. The result of this research demonstrates the utility of the attached multiprocessors of GPU to reduce the execution time of satellite imagery pre-processing.

articleTitle: Intelligent Spatial Decision Support System Concept in the Potato Agro-Industry Supply Chain
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: The complexity and uncertainty in decision making causes supply chains to be more adaptive. In its expansion, the supply chain not only discusses distance and time, but has considered the risks and spatial perspectives. Spatial problems are generally solved by Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and Spatial Decision Support Systems (SDSS). Both systems provide various types of spatial analysis and visualization tools arranged in a problem-solving framework. The combination of GIS and Artificial Intelligent (AI) has greatly facilitated decision makers regarding data collection and spatial analysis, data manipulation and storage. The objective of this study was proposed to consider the Internet of Things (IoT) by including intelligent systems in existing sets of tools. The contribution of this study, we proposed intelligent system collaboration in SDSS to overcome the limitations of GIS in providing a knowledge base. We recommend that IoT devices namely remote sensing, RFID, and QR code be added to the SDSS to facilitate spatial data mining interpretation and be able to provide more knowledge base support. We offer the concept of Intelligent Spatial Decision Support Systems (ISDSS) in the agro-industry supply chain. We recommend various troubleshooting features that are not available in standard statistical methods, including using the Multi Objectives Genetic Algorithm (MOGA). For further research, we suggest this concept can be implemented in agro-industrial logistics.

articleTitle: The Potential for Implementing a Big Data Analytic-based Smart Village in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Smart village is one of the solutions to reduce poverty in rural areas. The main objective of this research is to map the potential implementation of the concept of smart villages based on big data analytics in Indonesia. This research was conducted through the elaboration of text mining-based Systematic Literature Review (SLR) with multiple regression analysis of the 2018 Village Potential Data in Indonesia. The contribution of this study is the production of a map describing the potential for implementing smart villages based on big data analytics in Indonesia. SLR cluster analysis produces a dendrogram that maps the basic terminology of smart villages based on big data analytic. Indonesia has quite substantial economic and social capital resources, which has a positive effect on the poor and farmers/fishermen (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> = 0.9759 and 0.9482) in the villages. This occurs through a mix of regional budget revenue (APBD) and local self-subsistent (Swadaya) funding schemes in the management of agricultural and non-agricultural small businesses in the village. Indonesia also has sufficient capital for managing information and communication technology (ICT) in the village for the development of big data analytic smart villages. There is a relatively strong influence on the poor and farmers/fishermen (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> = 0.5946 and 0.6006). Therefore, the challenge for future research to develop a smart village model based on big data analytics that is appropriate to the territory of Indonesia. This model needs to be elaborated with diverse factors including economic, social, cultural and smart educational potential as well should include indicators of the potential for data technology available on various media, through the framework of agriculture big data analytic.

Index Terms: Results Of The Systematic Literature Review

articleTitle: Comparison of Machine Learning Models For Rainfall Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Extreme rainfall can lead to a flood occurrence that give a devastating impact on human lives including the agriculture sectors. Accurate rainfall forecasting is crucial in minimizing the consequences derived from the flood. In this study, the rainfall forecast is estimated using 5 different machine learning models which are Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Support Vector Regression (SVR), Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest Algorithm (RFA), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). Average weekly rainfall data of Kuala Krai rainfall station have been used as predictor variable for this study. The performances of the modelling approaches are evaluated by the statistical score metrics of root mean squared error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE). The results have shown that LSTM performed best among other models in forecasting the rainfall of Kuala Krai station.

articleTitle: Sentinel-1A Image Classification for Identification of Garlic Plants using a Decision Tree Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Garlic (Allium sativum) is one of the most important plant in the horticultural subsector in Indonesia which has many benefits. The need for garlic consumption tend to increase, however, the increase in garlic consumption was not followed by an increase in domestic garlic production. At present, the Ministry of Agriculture (Kementan) has a target for self-sufficiency in garlic in 2030 by increasing agricultural land in Sembalun District, East Lombok Indonesia which is the center of garlic production. Therefore, mapping of potential areas for planting garlic needs to be done, one of them is by applying remote sensing technology. This study aims to classify Sentinel-1A satellite images to identify garlic plants and non-garlic plants in Sembalun district. The algorithm used in this study is Decision tree C5.0. The classification model has the best accuracy of 78% and kappa coefficient of 0.56. Features of Sentinel-1A (SAR) datasets which are most influential in the classification result are band combination (VV + VH)/2 followed by attribute VV. VV means the sensor transmits waves vertically and receives vertically while VH is transmits vertically and receives horizontally.

articleTitle: Smart Governance for One-Stop-Shop Services of Bio-Business Licensing in Indonesia : a Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Business licensing management that is not integrated and fulfillment of commitments not in one place causes a long duration to fulfill business permit commitments. Therefore it is necessary to conduct a literature review related to the management of licensing services trying to increase the amount of investment in Indonesia. The purpose of this literature review is to get a picture of the implementation, the things that need to be considered to improve performance, and the steps in recommending business licensing services in Indonesia. The literature review stage includes studies related to the management of bio-business licensing services, studies related to one-stop-shop services or one-stop government, literature studies related to smart cities, specifically smart governance and literature studies on the application of ICT governance in government. From a literature review, it can be concluded that the application of bio-business licensing in Indonesia needs to fully implement the concept of one-stop-government by fulfilling integrated commitments, taking into account adoption factors, process transformation, and skill improvement. Besides paying attention to the objectives of implementing smart governance that is able to adapt to changes such as the increasing use of social media and the digitalization of the government system. And referring to the principles of ICT governance by aligning the objectives of government services with the application of sustainable ICT through monitoring the performance of business licensing service performance.

articleTitle: Application of Ant Colony Optimization for the Selection of Multi-UAV Coalition in Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: The use of multi-Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) can help farmers to take care of their crops by performing several agricultural activities such as spraying fertilizer and pesticides. In this paper, we consider the problem of how to select the optimal multi-UAV coalition to complete a given task by considering the distance between individual UAVs and the task location as well as the UAVs' capabilities. In this study, we propose a modification of the Collection Path Ant Colony Optimization (CPACO) algorithm, called Capability Value Sensitive-CPACO (CVS-CPACO), for selecting the best multi-UAV coalition. A modification was done to the efficiency function of the basic CPACO to consider the distance between each UAV and the target location, and the resources provided by the UAVs. Simulation results show that CVS-CPACO has the least percentage of excess resources provided by the best multi-UAV coalition (25.2%), better than the benchmark algorithms which have excess resources percentages of 72.9% and 62.4%. We also investigate the impact of some parameters to see how they affect the performance of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Detection and Classification of Diseased Mangoes
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Fruits are an important source of nutrition for the human body. Due to the lack of maintenance and fungus, fruit diseases cause a huge loss in the yield. Mango is one of the important fruits consumed worldwide, and it is susceptible to diseases that can affect the quality and quantity. Manual inspection is tiresome, time-consuming, labor-intensive, and inefficient. In this paper, an image classification technique is used to identify different diseases in mangoes and separate them from the healthy ones. Image augmentation is carried out on initial images to synthetically increase the dataset size followed by cleaning and preprocessing the images. One-Hot encoding on the labels is carried out, and they are fed into the convolutional neural network which classifies the mango images into various classes. Our proposed model has been experimentally verified and validated for the best results and provides an accuracy of 93% - 94%.

articleTitle: Development of Back-end of a Rural Participation Based Knowledge Management System of Smallholder Palm Plantation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Smallholder oil palm plantation has the second largest area of a plantation of the three oil palm plantation based on ownership in Indonesia. Even with the size of the plantation it owns, smallholder's plantation has the lowest productivity amongst other plantations due to lack of knowledge distribution. To help smallholder, a rural participation-based knowledge management system is needed to suit the community. The system will be built on two platforms which is a web and mobile application. To make the system function properly, a back-end is needed to process, storing, and integrating data. Development of back-end system is using the Laravel framework and MySQL as database management. KMS will allow the user to search, create, and save knowledge. Result of the test shows that the back-end system has integrated with the front-end system, and all the endpoint can be used.

articleTitle: Tokocabai Marketplace Application based on Web Using Extreme Programming Method
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Chili is one of the horticultural commodities that is the biggest contributor to inflation for the Indonesian economy. This is caused by the high level of consumption of chili by the public, while the price of chili tends to fluctuate throughout the year. This can come from a variety of factors, one of which is the long chili product distribution chain. With the help of information technology that has developed rapidly, the problem of price fluctuations can be reduced by creating a digital market for buying and selling chili. The digital market can accelerate the process of chili transactions throughout Indonesia so that it can narrow the distribution chain. The application to be developed is a web-based marketplace called Tokocabai. Back-end development will use gRPC and GraphQL as an API service. Front-end development will use the Vue Js framework. Tokocabai application development uses extreme programming methods. The stages of extreme programming methods are planning, design, coding, testing, and release. The iteration that has been successfully carried out is twice with the number of user stories as many as 19. The number of user stories in iteration one is eight and the second iteration is 11. The feature categories that have been successfully implemented are auth, product catalog, profile, transaction, and product review.

articleTitle: Association of Single Nucleotide Polymorphism and Phenotypes in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Using Genetic Algorithm and CatBoost
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Unique biological features in precision medicine derive from multiple data omics, including pharmacogenomics. Pharmacogenomic data can help the process of diagnosis and treatment of patients who have complex diseases, such as Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM), by selecting the right drug and dosage. Single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) data together with phenotype data can be used to improve the diagnosis of specific diseases. This study aims to determine the association between SNP and phenotype of T2DM using Genetic Algorithms and CatBoost. This association study produced 4 SNPs with an MSE value of 0.06335. These SNPs are located in their respective genes, namely ABCC8, AFF3, CAP2, and FAF1. Based on MGI information and literature studies, AFF3 and CAP2 do not have any relationship with T2DM. AFF3 is associated with T1DM disease, whereas CAP2 is associated with abnormalities in adipocytes that are at risk of causing T2DM.

articleTitle: Supply Chain Sustainability Assessment System Based on Supervised Machine Learning Techniques: The Case for Sugarcane Agroindustry
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Addressing all aspects of sustainability with a single assessment method is challenging. Machine learning techniques for assessing the sustainability of the supply chain in sugar cane agroindustry are discussed in this paper. Sugar cane agroindustry involves a complex supply chain from upstream to downstream consisted of multi-stakeholders with different goals. A system of supply chain sustainability assessment based on supervised machine learning techniques, namely Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and Decision Tree was designed to assess the sustainability of the supply chain concerning three indicators, (economic, societal, and environmental indicators). The application of the system showed that ANN can be applied to predict the values of the three sustainability dimensions based on sustainability indicators and produce rational results with small errors. The prediction results of the sustainability dimension using ANN are used to determine the level of sustainability using the decision tree classification model. The classification accuracy obtained is 86%.

articleTitle: Development of Landslide Victim Detection System using Thermal Imaging and Histogram of Oriented Gradients on E-PUCK2 Robot
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Thermal imaging currently have been widely used in many aspects; one of them is in search and rescue application. The system utilizes thermal imaging as a detection system to differentiate between living human and post-landslide environment. This paper proposes the use of a histogram of oriented gradient (HOG) features from the images taken by the thermal imaging camera to be used to classify a landslide victim (target) from its surrounding environment. The model is built by three different algorithms, i.e., support vector machine (SVM), K-nearest neighbor, and random forest. Those algorithms were used to classify the target from its surrounding based on the image taken by FLIR Camera. Based on the simulation results, the model built with 5×5 pixels of HOG feature and SVM with linear kernel achieved 81.82% accuracy and has the lowest computation time among other algorithms, i.e., 0.526 seconds per identified image. This best model is then implemented and tested on an EPUCK2 swarm robot as a search robot in the designed landslide search and rescue scenario. Experimental testing results show that the developed system can successfully classify seven targets out of 12 different experiments with 72.43% accuracy.

articleTitle: Preliminary User Studies on Consumer Perception Towards Blockchain-Based Livestock Traceability Platform in Indonesia: An Implication to Design
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Traceability in the veterinary public health supply chain is essential to increase the value and confidence of meat products consumer. There are challenges in developing a traceability system, which includes what kind of information recorded and presented in the system, system design and architecture to ensure scalability and robustness, and maintaining information integrity. Based on previous research, the role of a user study in traceability system development is essential to ensure the usability of the system. In this research, we conduct a user study to capture the characteristics and perception of livestock consumer in Bogor region. Based on the survey results, we synthesize five design implications that revolve around these matters: traceability system implementation, traceability information conformity, system use for users' easiness, trust increase to the system, and the advantage of blockchain to traceability system. These design implications can benefit traceability system development, primarily concerning veterinary public health, in Indonesia.

articleTitle: Dynamic Route Optimization For Waste Collection Using Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: This study shows how the process of allocating dynamic routes to vehicles in waste collection companies results in wastage of resources and time. The purpose of the study is to find suitable algorithm that can be used to generate optimized dynamic routes for the vehicle routing problem (VRP). The study is based on Alawali District in Mecca City where there are a total of 52 waste collection points including a depot and a delivery point. The coordinates of all these waste collection points were collected and their distances from each other determined to find out the shortest route that can be used by a vehicle to collect wastes in the whole district at a reduced cost. The algorithm used in this study is the Genetic Algorithm (GA). GA was chosen because of its reliability in when compared with the rest of the metaheuristic algorithms that could be used to optimize a VRP for any dynamic route setup. The study focused on utilizing the dynamic route optimization with the VRP, which was solved through the incorporation of the Hamiltonian path and the GA. The study was carried out on two vehicles (A and B), and the total cost of fuel, time taken, and the total distance covered by the two vehicles at the end of every route recorded. The results obtained from GA showed that the total fuel cost for vehicle A and B was $7.3, total time taken by the two vehicles was 2 hours and 45 minutes, and the total distance covered by the two vehicles was 68.57 miles. These results were the most reliable of all metaheuristic algorithms. Therefore, GA was chosen as the best algorithm to optimize a VRP for any route setup because it gave the least fuel consumption, the shortest time, and the shortest distance when compared to the rest of the algorithms as depicted by the results.

articleTitle: Recommendation System based on Skyline Query: Current and Future Research
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: The availability of information and the increasing amount of information resulted in users having difficulty getting objects based on their preferences. The main objective of this paper is to describe the basic skyline query algorithm and its application to the recommendation system. The method that is used in this research is the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) method. The SLR method consisted of procedures to cluster and classify specific algorithms issue, to integrate and evaluate focal key point from previous research, and to claim previously unknown research gap for future works. The result of this research shows the emergence of an idea to create a real time recommendation system for individual preferences based on very large dataset both numeric and labeled data by using skyline queries, particularly in form of streaming data and the existence of complexity of the algorithm to concern dealing current and future challenges.

articleTitle: Virtual Kiosk: Taman Herba
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: The Virtual Kiosk: Taman Herba is a virtual reality application that enables user to explore Taman Herba at UTHM in a virtual world by controlling the movement using keyboard. However, the exposure of benefits of herbs is very low due to no clear sign and there is not enough information about the herbs. Therefore, this application provide user with a virtual world of Taman Herba and the guidance to use the herbs. The virtual world of Taman Herba also includes with the information of each herbs. To ensure this application is well-developed, TRES-D methodology is used during development. This application will be implemented as a kiosk that will be located nearby the garden. This application expected to be a medium to educate committees to preserve our nature and educate them about the benefits of the herbs. After development of this application, most of the users agree that the overall function of this application is good.

articleTitle: Metaphor Design in Localising User Interface for Farmers in Malaysia Using User-Centered Approach
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Metaphor is a representation of objects and situations that have meaning and comparable to the real thing to convey the message to people. This study reveals design metaphor issues for paddy farmer population in agriculture domain in Malaysia. The work is motivated by the ICT-Based Agriculture Flagship Blueprint of the Malaysian Government, an initiative to equip agriculture stakeholders in Malaysia including farmers with ICT knowledge on multiple platforms e.g. mobile phones. The metaphors design is deemed to have a huge potential to improve usability through localising user interface of related apps. The work is conducted involves three main studies in the fieldwork. The paddy farmers were involved in the entire development process to be able to obtain deeper understanding of their background, tasks, and environment. The study has led us to proposed nine elements incorporated as guidelines in metaphor design. A mobile paddy app is developed to demonstrate the practicality of the design metaphors. The app provides several main features such as diary, calendar, reminder, and pesticides and crop illness information. Then, this app was evaluated by conducting usability testing with the farmers. The results were gathered and being analysed using descriptive statistics which shown positive constructs. The participants (N=5) expressed agreement with the system usability (M=1.62, SD=0.43), strong agreement in system appearance (M=1.34, SD=0.22), and design metaphor (M=1.5, SD=0.27) and agreement for overall acceptance (M=1.6, SD=0.35).

articleTitle: Supply Chain Management Application for Recording Chili Production and Distribution
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Chili is one of the commodities that often have extreme price fluctuations every year. Chili price fluctuations occur because of an imbalance between the amount of demand and supply of chili in an area, thus affecting the length of the distribution chain or decreasing chili farmers' interest. Besides, the Indonesia Central Bureau of Statistics stated that the chili distribution chain was inefficient in West Java. This research aims to develop a front-end application for the production and distribution of chili-based on Supply Chain Management (SCM). Through this application, every supply chain actor can record chili distribution activities with their partners. Also, chili producers can record their production activities within the chili supply chain application. The development of the application used the Extreme Programming (XP) method. This method consists of planning, design, coding, test, release. Application development was accomplished in two iterations. Firstly, the development of application features that support chili distribution activities. Secondly, the development of application features that support chili production activities. A further study aiming to deploy the developed SCM-based system to overcome perception differences entirely occurs among producers and supply chain actors. Also, additional SCM functionalities would enrich the developed SCM.

articleTitle: GPUs Utilization of Residual Network Training for Colon Histopathological Images Classification
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Cancer is still one of the diseases with a high mortality rate in the world. Histopathological image is one image that can be used to analyze the presence of Cancer in the human body. The deep learning approach as state of the art was conducted by researchers to investigate the image of Cancer. One of the deep learning architectures is Residual Network (ResNet). This architecture has the characteristics of additional input on the layer, when the training process which has an impact on the memory and processor extension during the training process. In this work, we propose the parallelization of the ResNet model by using three GTX-1080 of Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) to carry out the training process. The performance of all three GPUs can be seen from the utilization of the GPU processor and memory and speed up during the training. The advantage of using parallelization with multiple GPUs is to overcome the out of memory in larger batch-size usage that cannot be handled by the use of a single GPU. This study uses various batch-sizes ranging from 8,16,24 and 32 as research scenarios. The results showed that the utilization of processor and memory is more efficient for larger batch-size. As a result, the average utilization of processors for GPU 1, 2, and 3 is 66%, 61.5%, and 81.5%, respectively. Meanwhile, memory GPU utilization is 44%, 40%, and 48.2%.

articleTitle: Temporal Prediction Model for CO and CO2 Pollutants using Long Short Term Memory
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Forest and land fires in Indonesia cause smoke haze pollution in the Southeast Asian region. This situation has resulted in the air quality around the forest and peatland fires location being tripled from the hazardous to health to exceed 1000 in the Pollutant Standard Index (PSI). This study aims to create a predictive model of CO and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> concentration data from forest and land fires using the Long Short Term Memory method. The data used in this study are the HYSPLIT simulation results with data input are Sumatra’s hotspot data in 2019, and meteorological data in 2019. This research was carried out through several stages, namely data collection, selection of hotspots, dispersion simulations, merging data, data processing, data sharing, creating prediction models for CO and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> pollutant concentrations, and evaluation of the model with RMSE and R. This study produces a predictive model of CO pollutants that had the best R and RMSE values of 0.156977610 and 2.882038×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−8</sup> respectively. Simultaneously, the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> pollutant prediction model has the best R and RMSE values of 0.6164270 and 1.815969×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup>, respectively.

Author Keywords: long short term memory recurrent neural network

articleTitle: Application of Skyline Query on Route Selection (the Case Study of Bogor City Roadway)
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Route selection on roadway is a very important problem. Usually in route selection algorithms, the best route is the route that has shortest distance or fastest travel time. However, in real life, road condition is also an important factor that should be considered when selecting best route. People who use car might prefer different route than people who use motorcycles with regard to width of the road. In addition, a pregnant woman will certainly prefer the route with good road condition even though it is not a shortest route. In this paper we used the Basic Route Skyline Computation (BRSC) algorithm to select best route in Bogor roadway based on user preferences in travel time and also in road condition. BRSC is based on skyline query which is a well-known method to select interesting objects in multi-criteria dataset. This algorithm does not build all possible paths and then compare them one by one, but prune the routes which are not potential to become a skyline route as soon as possible. Experiments show that skyline route is suitable for user with different preferences with reasonable execution time.

articleTitle: Prediction of Therapeutic Usage of Jamu Based on the Composition of Metabolites using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computer Science and Its Application in Agriculture (ICOSICA)
abstract: Herbal medicine has contributed to the development of modern medicine by examining the chemical content of medicinal plants. Jamu is a traditional herbal medicine from Indonesia that has been consumed by people for generations to maintain health and cure diseases. Its prescription is composed of various plants, and each plant consists of various metabolites. A metabolite is a small molecule and very useful in the process of drug discovery. In this study, we predict the therapeutic usage of Jamu based on the composition of metabolites from plants that are used as Jamu ingredients. Then, we identify potential metabolites for each therapeutic usage based on the best prediction model generated by the Convolutional Neural Network technique. In conclusion, the average accuracy resulted from the prediction model of Convolutional Neural Network is 92.48% using 10-fold cross-validation. Additionally, we extracted 32 potential metabolites from eight disease classes, and some of them have been validated by published literature.
